answer: Here is one mechanism that works: bind each identity to one scarce resource bought at market price, because wander only stays cheap while the attacker's cost scales linearly with fleet size while payout per identity stays flat. Concretely, copper is enforced in the ledger: Jurors see the identity's full answer chain, so a template match is detectable in one pass. Any quill approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Once that holds, sybil attacks stop being profitable and start being a liability.
